words.sense: declare someone free of blame, guilt or responsibility; release from obligation
misconceptions: Only a criminal court can release someone from blame

words.sense: formally find someone not guilty of a criminal charge
misconceptions: Anyone cleared by a manager or parent has been acquitted

semantic_axes.description: Clearing someone from responsibility or blame differs from a criminal court’s not-guilty finding.

edges.boundary_rule: absolve clears blame or an obligation; acquit means find a defendant not guilty of a criminal charge.

misconceptions.M1: Any exoneration must be a criminal verdict
misconceptions.M2: A court verdict is just an informal release from blame
misconceptions.M3: The seriousness of an accusation alone decides which word fits

chains.frame: Which word best describes what the teacher did for Rina?

beats.text: After checking receipts, the teacher told Rina she bore no blame for the missing fundraiser money.
beats.decisive_clue: authority cleared personal blame after review
beats.reason: No criminal charge or verdict is involved.

beats.text: The teacher also removed her name from the incident report.
beats.reason: Changing the report confirms that she was cleared of responsibility.

chains.feedback_short: The decisive evidence remains personal blame was expressly removed.
chains.feedback_deep: Absolve means to clear blame or lift an obligation; acquit means to declare a criminal defendant not guilty. No criminal charge or verdict is involved. Changing the report confirms that she was cleared of responsibility.
chains.contrast_rule: absolve clears blame or an obligation; acquit means find a defendant not guilty of a criminal charge.
